body: Co-founder (1987, with Motilal Oswal) of Motilal Oswal Financial Services; author of the annual Motilal Oswal Wealth Creation Study since 1996 - the longest-running Indian dataset on which stocks created wealth and why. Early notable investments: Hero Honda, Infosys and Eicher Motors; his personal portfolio reportedly grew to ~Rs 100 crore by 2000 (Wikipedia; single-source). Hero Honda ranked first among the most consistent wealth creators in the 12th study (2002-07); Infosys, Hero Honda and Ranbaxy appeared in ten straight studies. Folklore (unverified): a ~Rs 10 lakh Hero Honda investment in the early 1990s grew to many crores. Process: QGLP - Quality (business and management), Growth (earnings growth runway), Longevity (how long growth and returns last), Price (reasonable vs growth) - plus 'Size' (small at the start, per the 100x study). The studies' core finding: big wealth comes from earnings growth plus P/E rerating, and buying at low P/E relative to future growth. Mistakes: Motilal Oswal's flagship MF schemes lagged badly in 2018-2021 when their quality-growth holdings de-rated and they missed cyclicals/PSUs (characterisation; check fund data). Copyable: the study PDFs are free - use their stock-level tables as a base-rate library (what % of wealth creators were small, at what P/E they started).

title: Raamdeo Agrawal - QGLP and the Wealth Creation Study (India)
